64e354980d44.content: World Health Organization (2022). Consolidated guidelines on HIV, viral hepatitis and STI prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care for key populations. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on HIV, viral hepatitis and STI prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care for key populations AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-7-22 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240052390 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guideline provides consolidated, evidence-based recommendations for the prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care of HIV, viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections (STIs) among key populations. It responds to the disproportionate burden of these infections in groups such as men who have sex with men, sex workers, people who inject drugs, people in prisons and other closed settings, and trans and gender diverse individuals, and to the structural barriers that limit their access to health services. The document aims to support countries in strengthening integrated, people-centred responses to these interconnected epidemics. Developed using WHO guideline standards and the GRADE methodology, the publication brings together existing and new recommendations and organizes them into comprehensive packages of interventions. It addresses enabling factors such as legal and policy environments, stigma, discrimination, violence and community empowerment, alongside essential health interventions including prevention, testing, treatment and harm reduction. The guideline also outlines service delivery approaches, such as community-led services, integration and decentralization, and provides guidance for programme planning, implementation and monitoring. Intended for policy-makers, programme managers and health-care providers, it supports the prioritization of effective, context-appropriate strategies to improve access, coverage and health outcomes for key populations. 77f7a21fcb20.content: World Health Organization (2026). National health workforce accounts: health workforce levels and trends 2026. World Health Organization. TitleNational health workforce accounts: health workforce levels and trends 2026 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-6-22 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240122925 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis report presents the 2026 edition of the National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) series, providing an overview of the status of NHWA implementation and an analysis of global and regional health workforce levels and trends based on official data reported by countries to the World Health Organization. Developed to support evidence-informed health workforce policy-making and planning, the report examines progress in strengthening national health workforce information systems, data availability and reporting across countries, and the use of standardized indicators to monitor human resources for health in support of universal health coverage, the Sustainable Development Goals and other health objectives. Drawing on the 2025 NHWA data release, the report analyses the distribution, density and composition of the health and care workforce across regions and income groups, highlighting persistent disparities in workforce availability. It also examines trends in workforce growth since 2006 and presents a thematic analysis of population ageing and health workforce ageing, assessing their implications for future workforce needs. The findings demonstrate substantial improvements in the availability and quality of health workforce data through NHWA implementation while underscoring continuing challenges related to workforce shortages, inequities in distribution and the need for sustained investment in health workforce planning and monitoring. TitleGuidelines for the prevention and control of infection with LAV/HTLV III AuthorsWorld Health Organization. Control Programme on AIDS Issued1986-12-31 Typedocument PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThese guidelines provide recommendations for preventing and controlling infection with LAV/HTLV-III, the retrovirus recognized at the time as the etiological agent of acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). Developed as part of the WHO AIDS Control Programme, they are intended primarily for public health authorities and health professionals, who are responsible for adapting the guidance to different populations and settings. The document summarizes available knowledge on transmission, clinical manifestations, laboratory detection, surveillance, notification and confidentiality, and case definitions for AIDS. The guidelines emphasize routine precautions to prevent exposure to blood and other potentially infectious body fluids, particularly among health care workers, laboratory personnel and providers of home and emergency care. They address prevention and management of needlestick, parenteral and mucous-membrane exposures, safe handling of specimens and contaminated equipment, and precautions for non-health-care workers. Guidance is also provided on disinfection, sterilization, and the safe processing of reusable needles, syringes and other instruments. deafca038250.doc: Directriz de la OMS: recomendaciones sobre intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud
deafca038250.title: Directriz de la OMS: recomendaciones sobre intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud
deafca038250.content: Organización Mundial de la Salud (2022). Directriz de la OMS: recomendaciones sobre intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud. Organización Mundial de la Salud. TitleDirectriz de la OMS: recomendaciones sobre intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud AuthorsOrganización Mundial de la Salud Issued2022-5-19 Typebook PublisherOrganización Mundial de la Salud ISBN9789240046993 (versión electrónica) Languagees AbstractEste documento presenta las recomendaciones de la OMS, basadas en la evidencia, sobre el uso de intervenciones digitales para fortalecer los sistemas de salud y apoyar el avance hacia la cobertura sanitaria universal (CSU). Elaborada en respuesta a la creciente adopción de las tecnologías digitales y a la resolución sobre salud digital aprobada por la Asamblea Mundial de la Salud en 2018, la directriz aborda la necesidad de evaluar rigurosamente las intervenciones de salud digital para garantizar que las inversiones se fundamenten en evidencia sobre sus beneficios, riesgos, aceptabilidad, factibilidad, implicaciones en materia de recursos y consideraciones de equidad. Asimismo, subraya que las tecnologías digitales deben complementar, y no sustituir, los componentes fundamentales de unos sistemas de salud sólidos y eficaces. Las recomendaciones se centran en un conjunto priorizado de intervenciones de salud digital accesibles, como mínimo, mediante dispositivos móviles, entre ellas la notificación de nacimientos y defunciones, la notificación de existencias y la gestión de suministros, la telemedicina entre pacientes y profesionales y entre profesionales, la comunicación dirigida a los pacientes, el seguimiento digital del estado de salud y de los servicios recibidos, las herramientas de apoyo a la toma de decisiones para el personal sanitario y el aprendizaje digital para los trabajadores de la salud. La directriz también presenta consideraciones para la implementación, identifica las principales lagunas de investigación y proporciona orientación a los ministerios de salud, los responsables de salud pública, los asociados para el desarrollo y otras partes interesadas para adoptar, ampliar e institucionalizar intervenciones de salud digital eficaces sobre la base de la mejor evidencia disponible. 93267234b1d8.content: World Health Organization (2020). Consolidated guidelines on HIV testing services, 2019. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on HIV testing services, 2019 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2020-11-3 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241550581 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guideline provides comprehensive, evidence-based recommendations to support countries in delivering high-quality, person-centred HIV testing services (HTS) across diverse populations and settings. Updating and consolidating previous WHO guidance issued in 2015 and 2016, it incorporates new evidence on HIV self-testing, social network-based HIV testing approaches, western blotting, and strategic service delivery to strengthen progress towards global HIV targets. Developed using the GRADE methodology and informed by systematic reviews, modelling studies and expert consultation, the guideline aims to improve the effectiveness, efficiency and quality of HIV testing while promoting timely linkage to prevention, treatment and care. The publication addresses the full continuum of HIV testing services, including demand creation, pre- and post-test services, facility- and community-based testing, implementation considerations for priority populations, strategic planning, diagnostic testing strategies, quality assurance and programme monitoring. It provides updated recommendations on HIV self-testing, provider-assisted referral, social network-based approaches and the use of dual HIV/syphilis rapid diagnostic tests, while emphasizing the WHO 5Cs of HIV testing services: consent, confidentiality, counselling, correct results and connection. Intended for policy-makers, national programme managers, health-care providers and implementing partners, the guideline supports the expansion of equitable, evidence-informed HIV testing services to improve diagnosis and strengthen national HIV responses. b2798db6c8b2.title: Guidelines: updated recommendations on HIV prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral initiation and monitoring
b2798db6c8b2.content: World Health Organization (2021). Guidelines: updated recommendations on HIV prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral initiation and monitoring. World Health Organization. TitleGuidelines: updated recommendations on HIV prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral initiation and monitoring AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-3-17 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240022232 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guideline presents updated WHO recommendations on selected priority areas across the HIV prevention, diagnosis and treatment continuum, developed in response to emerging evidence, implementation experience and evolving clinical practice. Prepared according to WHO Guideline Review Committee procedures and informed by systematic reviews using the GRADE approach, it updates and complements the 2016 consolidated HIV guidelines. The publication addresses key public health challenges affecting the global HIV response, particularly in resource-limited settings, and supports progress towards ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030 through a public health approach to service delivery. The guideline introduces or updates recommendations on the use of the dapivirine vaginal ring as an additional HIV prevention option for women at substantial risk of infection, point-of-care technologies for infant HIV diagnosis and viral load monitoring, revised treatment monitoring algorithms, and earlier initiation of antiretroviral therapy for people living with HIV and tuberculosis. It also provides updated clinical considerations for rapid antiretroviral therapy initiation and outlines implementation principles to support national adaptation. Intended for policy-makers, programme managers, clinicians and implementing partners, the guideline aims to strengthen evidence-based HIV prevention, diagnosis, treatment monitoring and care across diverse settings. World Health Organization. TitleGlobal guidance on criteria and processes for validation: elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B virus AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-11-25 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240039360 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guidance document provides updated World Health Organization criteria and processes for validating the elimination of mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT) of HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B virus (HBV) as public health priorities. Building on previous editions focused on HIV and syphilis, this third version incorporates validation guidance for HBV within the framework of the Triple Elimination Initiative. The document outlines standardized indicators, targets and assessment procedures for evaluating progress towards EMTCT across diverse epidemiological and programmatic settings. It addresses impact and process indicators, surveillance and laboratory quality standards, programme assessment, and requirements related to human rights, gender equality and community engagement. The document emphasizes integrated maternal and child health approaches, universal access to quality antenatal and prevention services, and the importance of strong health systems and surveillance mechanisms. It also provides guidance for countries with high disease burdens through the Path to Elimination framework, as well as for countries with small numbers of affected pregnant women and special populations. Intended for national, regional and global validation bodies, the document supports harmonized validation processes while allowing countries to pursue single, dual or triple EMTCT validation according to national readiness and regional priorities. d109c0764fde.content: World Health Organization (2021). WHO guideline for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions for cervical cancer prevention. World Health Organization. TitleWHO guideline for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions for cervical cancer prevention AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-7-6 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240030824 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis second edition of the WHO guideline provides updated evidence-based recommendations for screening and treatment of cervical pre-cancer lesions to prevent cervical cancer in both the general population of women and women living with HIV. Developed in support of the WHO global strategy to eliminate cervical cancer as a public health problem, the guideline responds to advances in screening technologies and implementation approaches by updating previous recommendations and introducing new guidance to simplify clinical algorithms while improving feasibility, acceptability and programme performance across diverse health system settings. The recommendations were developed in accordance with WHO guideline development procedures using systematic reviews, mathematical modelling where necessary, GRADE assessments of the certainty of evidence, evidence-to-decision frameworks, and consideration of feasibility, costs, acceptability and users’ values and preferences. The guideline presents recommendations and good practice statements on primary screening tests, screening intervals, age at initiation and cessation of screening, triage strategies, follow-up after positive screening results, treatment approaches, and programme implementation for both population groups. It addresses service delivery, integration with HIV care, implementation considerations, research gaps and dissemination, while emphasizing the transition to HPV DNA testing, the use of evidence-based screening and treatment algorithms, and country adaptation according to available resources and local context to improve coverage, quality of care and cervical cancer prevention. a6747b29d711.content: World Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe (2008). 8th National Tuberculosis Programme Managers Meeting and 13th Wolfheze Workshop: Wolfheze 2008: tuberculosis management, surveillance and evaluation in Europe with high rates or threat of multidrug resistant tuberculosis: The Hague, the Netherlands, 1–2 June 2008. World Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe. Title8th National Tuberculosis Programme Managers Meeting and 13th Wolfheze Workshop: Wolfheze 2008: tuberculosis management, surveillance and evaluation in Europe with high rates or threat of multidrug resistant tuberculosis: The Hague, the Netherlands, 1–2 June 2008 AuthorsWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe Issued2008-12-31 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe Languageen AbstractThe WHO European Region has the highest rates in the world of drug-resistant tuberculosis and increasing rates of HIV/tuberculosis coinfection. Eighteen high-priority countries have been identified to urgently scale up tuberculosis control interventions: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Bulgaria, Estonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Lithuania, the Republic of Moldova, Romania, the Russian Federation, Tajikistan, Turkey, Turkmenistan, Ukraine and Uzbekistan. Five of these countries are members of the European Union. Migration and pockets of poverty increase vulnerability to tuberculosis in many western European countries. Related areas, such as the rapid detection of drug-resistant tuberculosis, contact tracing, infection control, health system strengthening and the review of national tuberculosis programmes, are of equal concern among eastern, central and western countries of the WHO European Region. While general awareness and political commitment were raised during the Ministerial Forum held in Berlin in October 2007, how to ensure the follow-up of the Berlin Declaration on TB and monitor its implementation is currently under discussion. The 8th National Tuberculosis Programme Managers Meeting and the 13th Wolfheze Workshop, jointly organized in June 2008 in The Hague, provided a forum for discussion on each of the aforementioned topics and facilitated the sharing of experiences between countries in the Region – which are very different from an epidemiological, organizational, cultural and wealth perspective. ad697a1a92cf.content: World Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe (2014). The case for investing in public health: the strengthening public health services and capacity. A key pillar of the European regional health policy framework Health 2020. World Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe. TitleThe case for investing in public health: the strengthening public health services and capacity. A key pillar of the European regional health policy framework Health 2020 AuthorsWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe Issued2014-12-31 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for Europe Languageen AbstractThe economic crisis has led to increased demand and reduced resources for health sectors. The trend for increasing healthcare costs to individuals, the health sector and wider society is significant. Public health can be part of the solution to this challenge. The evidence shows that prevention can be cost-effective, provide value for money andgive returns on investment in both the short and longer terms. This public health summary outlines quick returns on investment for health and other sectors for interventions that promote physical activity and healthy employment; address housing and mental health; and reduce road traffic injuries and violence. Vaccinations and screening programmes are largely cost-effective. Population-level approaches are estimated to cost on average five times less than individual interventions. This report gives examples of interventions with early returns on investment and approaches with longer-term gains. Investing in cost-effective interventions to reduce costs to the health sector and other sectors can help create sustainable health systems and economies for the future. 74ea2ed4868a.doc: WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents
74ea2ed4868a.title: WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents
74ea2ed4868a.content: World Health Organization (2022). WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents. World Health Organization. TitleWHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-3-18 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240046832 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis operational handbook provides practical guidance for implementing World Health Organization recommendations on the prevention, screening, diagnosis and management of tuberculosis (TB) in children and adolescents under programmatic conditions and across different levels of the health system. Developed alongside the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, the publication addresses the specific epidemiological, clinical and psychosocial vulnerabilities of children and adolescents affected by TB, including challenges related to diagnosis, treatment adherence, prevention and continuity of care. The handbook aims to support the development and revision of national policies, operational guidance and service delivery approaches tailored to the needs of these populations. The handbook covers the full continuum of TB care, including contact investigation, systematic screening, preventive treatment, diagnostic approaches for pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB, and treatment of drug-susceptible and drug-resistant disease. It also addresses decentralized and family-centred models of care, management of TB in children and adolescents living with HIV, TB during pregnancy, malnutrition, pneumonia, adolescent health needs and palliative care. Practical tools, implementation guidance and standard operating procedures are included to support programme managers and health-care providers in strengthening child and adolescent TB services. b63d5fb2a9b2.doc: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease
b63d5fb2a9b2.title: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease
b63d5fb2a9b2.content: World Health Organization (2021). WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease. World Health Organization. TitleWHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 2: screening: systematic screening for tuberculosis disease AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-3-22 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240022676 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractTuberculosis remains one of the leading causes of death from a single infectious agent despite being largely preventable and curable. This updated WHO guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on systematic screening for tuberculosis disease to support earlier diagnosis, timely initiation of treatment and reduced transmission. It revises the 2013 guidance in light of new evidence on the effectiveness of screening interventions and the performance of screening tools, using the GRADE approach to assess the certainty of evidence and the strength of recommendations. The document is intended to assist countries in planning and implementing screening strategies adapted to their epidemiological and health system contexts. The guideline presents recommendations for systematic screening in the general population and in groups at increased risk of tuberculosis, including people living with HIV, household contacts, prisoners, miners, migrants and other vulnerable populations. It also reviews the use of symptom screening, chest radiography, computer-aided detection software, C-reactive protein and molecular WHO-recommended rapid diagnostic tests as screening tools, together with guidance on monitoring, evaluation and implementation considerations. The publication identifies research gaps and is accompanied by an operational handbook providing practical guidance for applying the recommendations in national tuberculosis programmes. ff1385343a0d.doc: Consolidated guidelines on person-centred HIV strategic information: strengthening routine data for impact
ff1385343a0d.title: Consolidated guidelines on person-centred HIV strategic information: strengthening routine data for impact
ff1385343a0d.content: World Health Organization (2022). Consolidated guidelines on person-centred HIV strategic information: strengthening routine data for impact. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on person-centred HIV strategic information: strengthening routine data for impact AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-7-28 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240055315 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThese consolidated guidelines provide normative guidance for strengthening HIV strategic information through person-centred routine data systems that support both clinical care and programme management. Developed in response to persistent gaps in HIV prevention, testing, treatment and retention despite substantial progress in the global HIV response, the guidelines promote the collection and use of individual-level longitudinal data to improve continuity of care, strengthen linkage across services and enhance monitoring of programme performance. They consolidate and update previous WHO guidance while introducing recommendations on person-centred monitoring, digital health information systems, interoperability, data quality, surveillance and the integration of HIV services with tuberculosis, viral hepatitis, sexually transmitted infections and other related conditions. The publication outlines recommendations and operational guidance on HIV prevention monitoring, patient monitoring, surveillance, digital health data, routine data use, priority indicators and implementation considerations. It emphasizes the transition from aggregate reporting to person-centred, digital information systems that support clinical decision-making, programme improvement and public health action while ensuring data privacy, confidentiality and security. The guidelines also describe minimum datasets, standardized monitoring tools and approaches to improving data quality and using routine information to strengthen service delivery and measure progress towards global HIV targets. 414cfc61ebc9.content: World Health Organization (2012). WHO recommendations: optimizing health worker roles to improve access to key maternal and newborn health interventions through task shifting. World Health Organization. TitleWHO recommendations: optimizing health worker roles to improve access to key maternal and newborn health interventions through task shifting AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2012-12-19 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241504843 Languageen AbstractThis WHO guidance provides evidence-based recommendations on optimizing health worker roles through task shifting to improve universal access to key maternal and newborn health interventions. Developed in response to health workforce shortages and inequities in access to care, it assesses whether specific interventions can be delivered safely and effectively by different health worker cadres, including lay health workers, auxiliary nurses and nurse midwives, nurses, midwives, associate clinicians, advanced level associate clinicians and non-specialist doctors. The guidance presents 119 recommendations, ranging from practices recommended for implementation to those requiring targeted monitoring and evaluation, rigorous research, or not recommended. It emphasizes that task shifting should complement efforts to increase skilled care and should aim to expand access while maintaining safety. Implementation should consider health-system capacity and local sociocultural, political and financial conditions, with recommendations adapted through national dialogue and considered as packages of interventions rather than in isolation. 1f7503cb7ae7.doc: The use of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis: policy guidance
1f7503cb7ae7.title: The use of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis: policy guidance
1f7503cb7ae7.content: World Health Organization (2016). The use of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis: policy guidance. World Health Organization. TitleThe use of loop-mediated isothermal amplification (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis: policy guidance AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2016-8-8 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241511186 Languageen AbstractTuberculosis remains a major global public health challenge, and the WHO End TB Strategy emphasizes the need for early diagnosis and universal drug-susceptibility testing. This policy guidance presents evidence-based recommendations on the use of the commercial loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay (TB-LAMP) for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis. Developed following a systematic review of studies conducted since 2012 and assessment using the GRADE approach, the document evaluates the diagnostic accuracy of TB-LAMP as a replacement for sputum-smear microscopy, as an add-on test after negative smear microscopy, and in comparison with the Xpert MTB/RIF assay, while also assessing the frequency of indeterminate or invalid results. Based on the available evidence, WHO recommends that TB-LAMP may be used as a replacement for sputum-smear microscopy in adults with signs and symptoms of pulmonary tuberculosis and as a follow-on test when further investigation of smear-negative specimens is required. The guidance emphasizes that these conditional recommendations are based on very low-quality evidence, apply to sputum specimens from patients with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis, and should not replace rapid molecular tests capable of detecting rifampicin resistance. It also highlights the limited evidence for use in people living with HIV, notes the extrapolation of recommendations to children, and provides implementation considerations and priorities for future research. e83273c4ab5c.content: منظمة الصحة العالمية (2024). تصنيف التدخلات والخدمات والتطبيقات الرقمية في مجال الصحة: لغة مشتركة لوصف استخدامات التكنولوجيا الرقمية من أجل الصحة. منظمة الصحة العالمية. Titleتصنيف التدخلات والخدمات والتطبيقات الرقمية في مجال الصحة: لغة مشتركة لوصف استخدامات التكنولوجيا الرقمية من أجل الصحة Authorsمنظمة الصحة العالمية Issued2024-10-8 Typebook Publisherمنظمة الصحة العالمية ISBN9789240093768 (نسخة إلكترونية) Languagear Abstractتقدم هذه الطبعة الثانية من «تصنيف التدخلات والخدمات والتطبيقات الرقمية في مجال الصحة» تصنيفاً معيارياً يصف كيفية استخدام التقنيات الرقمية لتلبية احتياجات الأفراد والنظم الصحية. وقد أعدت منظمة الصحة العالمية هذا التصنيف ليكون لغة مشتركة تدعم التواصل بين صانعي السياسات، ومديري البرامج الصحية، والباحثين، والمنفذين، ومطوري التكنولوجيا، وغيرهم من أصحاب المصلحة في مجال الصحة الرقمية. وينظم التصنيف التدخلات الصحية الرقمية حول قدرات تكنولوجية محددة صُممت لمعالجة التحديات التي تواجه النظم الصحية، ويربط هذه التدخلات بالخدمات وأنواع التطبيقات الرقمية التي تُستخدم لتنفيذها. ويُحدِّث هذا المنشور ويوسِّع الطبعة الأولى الصادرة عام 2018 ليعكس التقدم في تقنيات الصحة الرقمية، وتطور ممارسات التنفيذ، والدروس المستفادة من استخدامها على المستوى العالمي. ويستند الإطار إلى ثلاثة محاور مترابطة: تحديات النظم الصحية، والتدخلات الصحية الرقمية، والخدمات وأنواع التطبيقات الرقمية. ويشمل تدخلات موجهة للأفراد، ولمقدمي الرعاية الصحية، ولمديري النظم الصحية، ولخدمات البيانات، إلى جانب فئات التطبيقات الرقمية ونظم المعلومات. ويهدف هذا التصنيف إلى دعم التخطيط والتنفيذ، وتحليل الاستثمارات، والبحوث، واعتبارات التشغيل البيني، وصياغة السياسات، وحوكمة مبادرات الصحة الرقمية، بما يعزز الاستخدام المنسق والفعال للتقنيات الرقمية في النظم الصحية. 7e0d86bdff0b.title: Global hepatitis report 2026
7e0d86bdff0b.content: World Health Organization (2026). Global hepatitis report 2026. World Health Organization. TitleGlobal hepatitis report 2026 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-4-24 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240122383 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis report provides a comprehensive assessment of the global burden of viral hepatitis and progress towards the goal of eliminating hepatitis as a public health threat by 2030. Drawing on data reported by Member States and modelled estimates, it analyses trends in incidence, prevalence and mortality associated with hepatitis B and C, covering the period from 2015 to 2024 based on the latest available data. It also situates these trends within the context of global commitments, strategies and targets. The publication reviews the coverage and impact of key interventions for prevention, diagnosis and treatment, including vaccination, infection prevention and control, harm reduction and access to antiviral therapies. It identifies persistent gaps in testing and treatment, marked regional disparities, and the need for accelerated scale-up of services, particularly in high-burden settings. The report concludes that progress towards the 2030 elimination targets remains off track despite the availability of effective interventions. Intended for policymakers, programme managers and public health stakeholders, it serves as an analytical and strategic resource to guide national and global responses to viral hepatitis. TitleWHO guidelines for screening and treatment of precancerous lesions for cervical cancer prevention AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2013-11-19 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241548694 Languageen AbstractThese guidelines provide recommendations for screen-and-treat strategies to prevent cervical cancer by detecting and treating precancerous cervical lesions. The screen-and-treat approach bases treatment decisions on screening results, allowing treatment soon or ideally immediately after a positive test, rather than requiring histological confirmation. The guidelines compare strategies using human papillomavirus (HPV) testing, visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA), and cytology, linked to treatment with cryotherapy or loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). They are intended primarily to support policy-makers, programme managers and other health professionals in selecting appropriate cervical cancer prevention strategies according to available resources and existing programmes. Nine recommendations are provided. HPV-based screening is generally preferred where feasible, while VIA is suggested where HPV testing is not feasible; cold knife conization is not recommended as part of a screen-and-treat strategy. Recommendations apply to all women, with specific guidance for women living with HIV. Decision-making and implementation flowcharts support adaptation of the recommended strategies to country and regional contexts. 15011b802778.doc: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 3: diagnosis: web annex B: evidence synthesis and analysis
15011b802778.title: WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 3: diagnosis: web annex B: evidence synthesis and analysis
15011b802778.content: World Health Organization (2025). WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 3: diagnosis: web annex B: evidence synthesis and analysis. World Health Organization. TitleWHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 3: diagnosis: web annex B: evidence synthesis and analysis AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2025-4-10 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization DOIhttps://doi.org/10.2471/B09341 Languageen AbstractThis web annex to the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, Module 3: Diagnosis, compiles the evidence synthesis and analyses used to inform WHO recommendations on diagnostic technologies for tuberculosis and drug-resistant tuberculosis. The publication presents systematic reviews, meta-analyses, qualitative evidence syntheses and economic evaluations examining the diagnostic accuracy, safety, cost–effectiveness and implementation considerations of multiple diagnostic approaches, including low- and moderate-complexity nucleic acid amplification tests, targeted next-generation sequencing technologies and Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigen-based skin tests. The annex describes the methods applied to identify, assess and synthesize evidence across diverse populations and settings, including adults, adolescents, children and people living with HIV. It addresses the detection of pulmonary and extrapulmonary tuberculosis, rifampicin resistance and multidrug-resistant tuberculosis using respiratory and non-respiratory specimens. The document also examines stakeholder and user perspectives, operational feasibility and factors influencing implementation. Developed in accordance with WHO guideline development standards, the annex provides the technical evidence base underpinning updates to WHO policy guidance on tuberculosis diagnosis and drug-resistance testing. Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex C: indicators table. World Health Organization. TitleDigital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex C: indicators table AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-12-14 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis web annex provides the standardized indicators and performance metrics supporting the WHO Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems. It defines a comprehensive set of indicators for monitoring HIV prevention, testing, treatment, care, diagnostics and programme performance, translating WHO recommendations into standardized indicator specifications that can be incorporated into digital health systems. For each indicator, the annex documents indicator definitions, calculation methods, numerators and denominators, disaggregation variables, required data elements, reporting requirements, data sources, implementation notes and mappings to international monitoring frameworks, including WHO, UNAIDS, Global Fund and PEPFAR indicators where applicable. Intended for programme managers, monitoring and evaluation specialists, digital health architects and software developers, this resource supports the standardized measurement, reporting and analysis of HIV programme performance while promoting interoperability, consistent implementation of WHO recommendations and adaptation to national monitoring requirements. 5c08554cd1ed.title: WHO guideline: recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening
5c08554cd1ed.content: World Health Organization (2019). WHO guideline: recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening. World Health Organization. TitleWHO guideline: recommendations on digital interventions for health system strengthening AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2019-4-16 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241550505 Languageen AbstractThis WHO guideline provides evidence-based recommendations on the use of digital interventions to strengthen health systems and support progress towards universal health coverage (UHC). Developed in response to the growing adoption of digital technologies and the 2018 World Health Assembly resolution on digital health, it addresses the need for rigorous evaluation of digital health interventions to ensure that investments are informed by evidence of their benefits, harms, acceptability, feasibility, resource implications and equity considerations. The guideline emphasizes that digital technologies should complement, rather than replace, the fundamental components of well-functioning health systems. The recommendations focus on a prioritized set of digital health interventions accessible at a minimum through mobile devices, including birth and death notification, stock notification and commodity management, client-to-provider and provider-to-provider telemedicine, targeted client communication, digital tracking of clients’ health status and services, health worker decision support, and digital learning for health workers. The guideline also outlines implementation considerations, identifies research gaps, and supports ministries of health, public health practitioners, development partners and other stakeholders in making evidence-based decisions on the adoption, scale-up and institutionalization of effective digital health interventions. cfe4ca6caa37.title: Toolkit for analysis and use of routine health facility data: integrated health services analysis: district and facil…
cfe4ca6caa37.content: World Health Organization (2023). Toolkit for analysis and use of routine health facility data: integrated health services analysis: district and facility level. World Health Organization. TitleToolkit for analysis and use of routine health facility data: integrated health services analysis: district and facility level AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-6-16 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240060609 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis guidance document, part of the WHO Toolkit for analysis and use of routine health facility data, provides practical guidance on the integrated analysis and use of routine health information system (RHIS) data at district and health facility levels. It is intended to support managers, analysts and other health system stakeholders in monitoring health service delivery and using routine data for operational decision-making. The document promotes an integrated, standards-based approach that uses a limited set of tracer indicators representing multiple programmes and service components, thereby supporting primary health care, universal health coverage and the health-related Sustainable Development Goals. The publication presents principles for RHIS data analysis, including integration across programmes, focused use of key indicators, standardization of analyses and visualizations, routine assessment of data quality, and purpose-oriented use of information for management and planning. It organizes indicators into three groups: health status and epidemiological profile, health service performance, and health service resources. For each group, the publication provides indicator definitions, metadata, recommended disaggregations, analytical approaches, and examples of dashboards and visualizations. It emphasizes the interpretation of routine data within local contexts and illustrates how standardized dashboards can support supervision, performance review, resource allocation and continuous improvement of health services at subnational levels. 664e0653055a.doc: National health workforce accounts: implementation guide
664e0653055a.title: National health workforce accounts: implementation guide
664e0653055a.content: World Health Organization (2018). National health workforce accounts: implementation guide. World Health Organization. TitleNational health workforce accounts: implementation guide AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2018-10-19 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241514446 Languageen AbstractThe National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) Implementation Guide provides practical guidance for countries on establishing and sustaining systems to collect, analyse, use and report standardized health workforce data. Developed as a companion document to the NHWA Handbook and in support of the Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030, the guide outlines a structured approach to strengthening health workforce information systems and improving the availability, quality and use of human resources for health data. It is intended for policy-makers, programme managers, technical experts and stakeholders involved in health workforce planning, monitoring and governance, and emphasizes collaboration across sectors such as health, education, labour, finance and statistics. The guide presents an implementation framework organized into three phases—conceptualization, operationalization, and scaling up and sustainability—comprising eight steps that address political commitment, governance arrangements, planning, legal considerations, data compilation and analysis, validation, dissemination, and process review. It describes the roles of national institutions and multistakeholder coordination mechanisms, provides guidance on data quality, reporting and communication processes, and promotes the integration of existing information systems. By supporting the systematic monitoring of health workforce indicators, the guide aims to strengthen evidence-informed decision-making and contribute to health workforce development, universal health coverage and broader national and global health objectives. 889313bd780e.content: World Health Organization (2023). Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex D: function and non-functional requirements. World Health Organization. TitleDigital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing: WHO recommendations in digital systems: web annex D: function and non-functional requirements AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-12-14 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis web annex provides the high-level functional and non-functional requirements supporting the WHO Digital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems. It translates WHO HIV recommendations and service delivery workflows into standardized system requirements to guide the design, development, procurement and implementation of interoperable digital health solutions. The annex defines functional requirements for key business processes across HIV prevention, testing, treatment, care, diagnostics, referral, follow-up and reporting, together with non-functional requirements addressing system performance, security, confidentiality, privacy, interoperability, usability, reliability and offline functionality. Structured as a software-neutral implementation resource, it enables consistent interpretation of operational requirements while allowing adaptation to national policies and digital health architectures. Intended for digital health architects, software developers, implementers, procurers and programme managers, this resource supports the development of standards-based HIV information systems that accurately implement WHO recommendations while ensuring robust, secure and sustainable digital health solutions. World Health Organization. TitlePoliovirus containment: guidance to minimize risk for facilities collecting, handling or storing materials potentially infectious for polioviruses: web annex A: country and area specific poliovirus data, April 2023 update AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-7-24 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis web annex provides updated country- and area-specific poliovirus circulation data to support the assessment of potentially infectious materials in facilities collecting, handling or storing samples that may contain polioviruses. It accompanies the second edition of Poliovirus containment: guidance to minimize risks for facilities collecting, handling or storing materials potentially infectious for polioviruses and is intended to assist facilities in identifying samples requiring appropriate risk mitigation or containment measures. The annex presents Table A2.1, which compiles poliovirus circulation dates by country and area, including wild poliovirus (WPV), vaccine-derived poliovirus (VDPV) and oral polio vaccine type 2/novel oral polio vaccine type 2/Sabin2 potentially infectious material periods. The data were derived from national poliovirus reports, systematic literature searches and consultations with WHO regional offices, and are regularly revised and updated. The information supports the identification and management of potentially infectious materials according to the containment requirements outlined in the accompanying guidance. 07013f98600c.doc: Use of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement
07013f98600c.title: Use of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement
07013f98600c.content: World Health Organization (2011). Use of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement. World Health Organization. TitleUse of tuberculosis interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in low- and middle-income countries : policy statement AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2011-12-31 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241502672 Languageen AbstractThis policy statement provides evidence-based recommendations on the use of commercial interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) for tuberculosis (TB) in low- and middle-income countries, particularly settings with a high TB and/or HIV burden. Based on systematic reviews and GRADE assessment, it evaluates IGRAs for diagnosis of active TB, detection of latent TB infection (LTBI) in children and people living with HIV, screening of health care workers and contacts, outbreak investigations, and prediction of progression to active disease. The evidence was generally of low or very low quality and did not demonstrate superior performance of IGRAs over the tuberculin skin test (TST). WHO recommends that IGRAs and the TST not be used to diagnose active TB or identify individuals at risk of developing active disease, and that IGRAs not replace the TST for LTBI diagnosis in children, people living with HIV, or contacts. Given comparable performance, greater cost and technical complexity, replacing the TST with IGRAs as a public health intervention in resource-constrained settings is not recommended. ee25150a1c33.title: Classification of digital interventions, services and applications in health: a shared language to describe the uses …
ee25150a1c33.content: World Health Organization (2023). Classification of digital interventions, services and applications in health: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for health. World Health Organization. TitleClassification of digital interventions, services and applications in health: a shared language to describe the uses of digital technology for health AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-10-24 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240081949 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis second edition of the Classification of Digital Interventions, Services and Applications in Health provides a standardized taxonomy for describing how digital technologies are used to address individual and health system needs. Developed by WHO, the classification establishes a shared language to support communication among policy-makers, health programme managers, researchers, implementers, technology developers and other stakeholders involved in digital health. It organizes digital health interventions around discrete technological capabilities designed to address health system challenges and links these interventions to the digital services and application types through which they are delivered. The publication updates and expands the first edition published in 2018 to reflect advances in digital health technologies, evolving implementation practices and lessons learned from global use. The framework is structured around three interconnected axes: health system challenges, digital health interventions and digital services and application types. It includes interventions for persons, health-care providers, health system managers and data services, alongside categories of digital applications and information systems. The classification is intended to support planning, implementation, investment analysis, research, interoperability considerations, policy development and the governance of digital health initiatives, thereby facilitating more consistent and effective use of digital technologies in health systems. dac51f4340d0.title: Contingency fund for emergencies: 2020 annual report
dac51f4340d0.content: World Health Organization (2021). Contingency fund for emergencies: 2020 annual report. World Health Organization. TitleContingency fund for emergencies: 2020 annual report AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-7-2 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractThis annual report presents an overview of the activities, financing and operational impact of the World Health Organization’s Contingency Fund for Emergencies (CFE) in 2020. The publication describes how the CFE enabled WHO to respond rapidly to 14 emergencies in 13 countries and to support the global response to COVID-19 through the release of nearly US$ 44 million. It outlines the Fund’s role in supporting outbreak control, emergency health operations, supply chain management, surveillance, vaccination activities, procurement of essential medical supplies and continuity of health services during infectious disease outbreaks, humanitarian crises, natural disasters and technological emergencies. The report highlights WHO-supported responses to the COVID-19 pandemic, Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Beirut port explosion, Tropical Cyclone Harold in Vanuatu and the humanitarian crisis in north-eastern Syria. It also examines funding allocations, reimbursement mechanisms, donor contributions and accountability arrangements governing the CFE. Through operational examples and financial analysis, the publication demonstrates the importance of rapid, flexible and predictable financing for strengthening emergency preparedness and enabling timely public health action in complex and evolving emergencies. 91dc03c06777.content: World Health Organization (2023). Pandemic influenza preparedness framework: annual progress report, 1 January – 31 December 2022. World Health Organization. TitlePandemic influenza preparedness framework: annual progress report, 1 January – 31 December 2022 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-8-4 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240076907 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThe Pandemic Influenza Preparedness (PIP) Framework: annual progress report, 1 January–31 December 2022 presents technical and financial progress in implementing the PIP Framework, which aims to strengthen the sharing of influenza viruses with human pandemic potential and improve developing countries’ access to pandemic vaccines and other response supplies. The report assesses progress under the High-Level Implementation Plan II (2018–2023), including activities financed through the industry-funded Partnership Contribution mechanism. The report documents achievements and challenges in influenza laboratory capacity and surveillance, virus sharing, disease burden estimation, regulatory preparedness, risk communication and community engagement, deployment planning, and national pandemic preparedness. In 2022, 91% of Partnership Contribution recipient countries reported influenza data to FluNet, 48 countries had implemented regulatory approaches for pandemic influenza products, and 37 countries had developed or updated pandemic preparedness plans. It also presents progress in securing pandemic response products through benefit-sharing agreements, alongside financial allocations, expenditures and implementation milestones. bda567d8e2e3.title: Classification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langag…
bda567d8e2e3.content: Organisation mondiale de la Santé (2024). Classification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langage commun pour décrire les diverses utilisations de la technologie numérique dans le domaine de la santé. Organisation mondiale de la Santé. TitleClassification des interventions, des services et des applications numériques dans le domaine de la santé : un langage commun pour décrire les diverses utilisations de la technologie numérique dans le domaine de la santé AuthorsOrganisation mondiale de la Santé Issued2024-9-12 Typebook PublisherOrganisation mondiale de la Santé ISBN9789240093720 (version électronique) Languagefr AbstractCette deuxième édition de la Classification des interventions, services et applications numériques en santé présente une taxonomie normalisée permettant de décrire la manière dont les technologies numériques sont utilisées pour répondre aux besoins des individus et des systèmes de santé. Élaborée par l’OMS, cette classification établit un langage commun destiné à faciliter la communication entre les décideurs, les responsables de programmes de santé, les chercheurs, les responsables de mise en œuvre, les développeurs de technologies et les autres acteurs du domaine de la santé numérique. Elle organise les interventions numériques en santé autour de capacités technologiques distinctes conçues pour répondre à des défis des systèmes de santé et relie ces interventions aux services et types d’applications numériques qui les mettent en œuvre. La publication met à jour et élargit la première édition publiée en 2018 afin de refléter les progrès des technologies de santé numérique, l’évolution des pratiques de mise en œuvre et les enseignements tirés de leur utilisation à l’échelle mondiale. Le cadre est structuré autour de trois axes interconnectés : les défis des systèmes de santé, les interventions numériques en santé et les services et types d’applications numériques. Il comprend des interventions destinées aux personnes, aux prestataires de soins, aux gestionnaires des systèmes de santé et aux services de données, ainsi que des catégories d’applications numériques et de systèmes d’information. Cette classification vise à soutenir la planification, la mise en œuvre, l’analyse des investissements, la recherche, l’interopérabilité, l’élaboration des politiques et la gouvernance des initiatives de santé numérique. a645f73033c3.content: World Health Organization (2020). WHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 1: prevention: tuberculosis preventive treatment. World Health Organization. TitleWHO operational handbook on tuberculosis: module 1: prevention: tuberculosis preventive treatment AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2020-3-23 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240002906 Languageen AbstractThis operational handbook provides practical guidance for the programmatic management and scale-up of tuberculosis preventive treatment (TPT) in line with WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis. The publication addresses the global burden of tuberculosis infection and the need to expand preventive interventions among populations at high risk of developing TB disease, particularly people living with HIV, household contacts of TB patients and other vulnerable groups. It supports implementation of commitments made at the United Nations High-Level Meeting on Tuberculosis and outlines strategies to strengthen national responses through integrated, people-centred approaches. The handbook describes the cascade of care for TPT, including identification of target populations, exclusion of active TB disease, testing for TB infection, treatment options, management of adverse events, adherence support, monitoring and evaluation, and ethical considerations. It also provides operational guidance for contact investigation, integration of preventive services with active TB case finding and HIV services, health system strengthening, and resource mobilization. Practical implementation tools, policy considerations and monitoring indicators are included to assist national TB programmes, policy-makers and health-care providers in adapting and scaling up TPT services in diverse epidemiological and health system settings. 4359ef1c18a2.doc: Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006
4359ef1c18a2.title: Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006
4359ef1c18a2.content: World Health Organization. Regional Office for South-East Asia (2006). Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006. WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia. TitleEnumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes : report of a workshop, Bangkok, Thailand, 6-10 June 2006 AuthorsWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for South-East Asia Issued2006-12-31 Typedocument PublisherWHO Regional Office for South-East Asia Languageen AbstractDescription: Enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes is essential for initiation of antiretroviral therapy for a person with HIV as well as for monitoring the response to treatment. The techniques for enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes are evolving. The flow cytometry continues to be the gold standard of CD4 T lymphocytes enumeration in spite of the fact that the technology is expensive both in terms of initial investment in sophisticated equipment and running cost. The newer techniques may be economical to procure and maintain. The latter are particularly intended for countries with limited resources. WHO conducted a workshop to orient the nationals about these technologies and integration of a quality system into routine testing, at Siriraj Hospital Bangkok. The report describes the status of CD4 testing in these countries. While Indonesia, India and Thailand have developed a good infrastructure for enumeration of CD4 T lymphocytes, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal and Sri Lanka have made a beginning in this direction. The workshop focussed on principles of various techniques and imparted a hands-on training for performing the same. The issues regarding selection of technology, procurement of equipment and their maintenance; ensuring continuous supply and economical use of reagents and biosafety in laboratory were discussed and have been presented in this Report. TitleDigital adaptation kit for HIV: operational requirements for implementing WHO recommendations in digital systems AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2023-12-21 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240085138 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis second edition of the digital adaptation kit for HIV provides operational, software-neutral requirements to support the incorporation of WHO clinical, public health and data use recommendations into digital systems. Developed within the SMART Guidelines approach, it focuses on the content requirements for person-centred digital tracking and decision support systems used by health workers for HIV services in primary health care settings. The kit is intended to facilitate transparent, consistent and adaptable translation of narrative guidance into digital implementations while supporting interoperability and local customization. The publication organizes HIV-related requirements into eight components: health interventions and associated recommendations; generic personas; illustrative user scenarios; business processes and workflows; core data elements; decision support and scheduling logic; indicators and performance metrics; and high-level functional and non-functional requirements. It covers processes including HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis, care and treatment, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, infant diagnosis, diagnostics, client follow-up, referral, and aggregate reporting and data use, with complementary operational resources provided in web annexes. 559c28029389.content: World Health Organization (2022). WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents. World Health Organization. TitleWHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis: module 5: management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2022-3-18 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240046764 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractTuberculosis (TB) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children and adolescents, with substantial gaps in case detection, diagnosis and access to preventive treatment worldwide. This guideline consolidates new and existing WHO recommendations for the management of TB in these populations, replacing the 2014 guidance and reflecting the latest evidence on prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and models of care. It aims to support countries in strengthening the continuum of TB care and improving health outcomes through evidence-based policies and practices tailored to the specific needs of children, adolescents and their families. The publication provides recommendations on TB screening and contact investigation, TB preventive treatment, diagnostic approaches, treatment of drug-susceptible and drug-resistant TB, management of TB meningitis, and decentralized, family-centred models of care. It incorporates updated evidence on the use of Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, integrated treatment decision algorithms, shortened treatment regimens for non-severe TB, and therapeutic options for multidrug- or rifampicin-resistant disease in children. Developed according to WHO guideline development standards, the document is intended for national TB programmes, policy-makers, health professionals and implementing partners, and contributes to global efforts to reduce TB-related morbidity and mortality in line with the End TB Strategy and Sustainable Development Goals. c9cce3db7a42.title: Consolidated HIV guidelines: service delivery
c9cce3db7a42.content: World Health Organization (2026). Consolidated HIV guidelines: service delivery. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated HIV guidelines: service delivery AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-7-22 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240124233 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractHIV remains a major public health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, despite the availability of effective treatment and prevention tools. Many evidence-based interventions are not implemented consistently or delivered in a timely manner, contributing to ongoing HIV transmission, advanced disease and preventable mortality. These consolidated WHO guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations to strengthen HIV service delivery through people-centred, integrated and equitable approaches that improve access to care, continuity of treatment and accelerate progress towards ending AIDS as a public health threat. The publication consolidates all WHO recommendations on HIV service delivery issued between 2013 and 2025. It is intended to support the development of national and subnational policies, clinical guidelines and implementation guidance. It addresses key components of HIV service delivery, including linkage to care and antiretroviral therapy initiation, clinical follow-up and medication refills, adherence support and re-engagement in care, services for adolescents and young people, task sharing, decentralized service delivery, and integration with maternal and child health, tuberculosis, sexual and reproductive health, diabetes, hypertension and mental health services. Recommendations are classified as new, updated or revalidated according to WHO guideline development procedures. c29f83e22609.title: Understanding national health workforce accounts
c29f83e22609.content: World Health Organization (2017). Understanding national health workforce accounts. World Health Organization. TitleUnderstanding national health workforce accounts AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2017-12-31 Typereport PublisherWorld Health Organization Languageen AbstractUnderstanding National Health Workforce Accounts (NHWA) is an introductory guidance document developed by the World Health Organization to explain the purpose, policy relevance and structure of the National Health Workforce Accounts framework. The publication outlines how NHWA supports the standardization of health workforce information systems, improves the quality and comparability of data, and strengthens the evidence base for health workforce policy, planning and monitoring. Positioned within the context of universal health coverage, the Sustainable Development Goals, the Global Strategy on Human Resources for Health: Workforce 2030, and related international commitments, the document highlights the importance of reliable workforce information for addressing current and future health system challenges. The publication describes the benefits of NHWA at national, regional and global levels and presents key policy questions that can be informed through systematic workforce data collection and analysis. It introduces the health labour market framework used by NHWA, emphasizing workforce production, labour market flows, distribution, productivity and regulation. The document also summarizes the development process of the NHWA indicators and explains the modular structure of the framework, which comprises ten modules covering workforce stock, education, labour market dynamics, employment conditions, financing, governance, planning and information systems. Together, these elements provide a foundation for evidence-informed decision-making and strengthened health workforce monitoring. a38ca9fa0aa0.title: Cost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republ…
a38ca9fa0aa0.content: Khadijeh Ezoji; Mohsen Yaghoubi; Marzieh Nojomi; et al. (2019). Cost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran. World Health Organization. Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean. TitleCost-effectiveness of introducing the pneumococcal conjugate vaccine for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran AuthorsKhadijeh Ezoji; Mohsen Yaghoubi; Marzieh Nojomi; Sussan Mahmoody; Seyed Mohsen Zahraie; Maziar Moradi-Lakeh; Sedigheh R. Tabatabaei; Abdollah Karimi Issued2019-10-29 Typedocument PublisherWorld Health Organization. Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean DOIhttps://doi.org/10.26719/emhj.19.039 Languageen AbstractBackground: Pneumococcal disease caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae results in considerable mortality and morbidity. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV), such as PCV-13, can prevent invasive pneumococcal disease and avoid disability and death. The cost of introducing PCV-13 in childhood immunization schedules should be assessed against the cost of pneumococcal diseases for each community. Aims: This study aimed to evaluate the cost–effectiveness of introducing PCV-13 in the national immunization programme for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran. Methods: The TRIVAC decision support model was used to estimate total costs of introducing PCV-13 and the disability-adjusted life years (DALYs)averted. The main pneumococcal diseases were considered—pneumonia, meningitis, acute otitis media, and non-pneumonia, non-meningitis infections—in terms of hospital admissions, outpatient visits and deaths. Local data were used to estimate costs. Results: Pneumococcal disease is estimated to affect 18 713 211 children under 5 years (519 412 pneumonia, 18 148 116 acute otitis media, 6884 meningitis, and 38 799 non-pneumonia, non-meningitis)in 10 years (2014–2023)without use of the vaccine. Introduction of PCV-13 would prevent 4 900 084 cases of pneumococcal disease (190 849 pneumonia, 4 692 450 acute otitis media, 2529 meningitis, and 14 256 non-pneumonia, non-meningitis). Pneumococcal infection would cause 287 950 hospital admissions and 29 399 deaths; vaccination could avert 105 802 hospital admissions and 9997 deaths. The incremental cost–effectiveness was estimated to be US$ 1890 and US$ 1538 per averted DALY for the government and society respectively. Conclusion: According to WHO-recommended thresholds for interpreting cost–effectiveness, introduction of PCV-13 for children under 5 years in the Islamic Republic of Iran would be cost-effective Sources . | iris.who.int/handle/10665/385346 (canonical) | doi:https://doi.org/10.26719/emhj.19.039 (doi) | repository record (repository) | . 2641c188b189.doc: Digital transformation handbook for reporting substandard and falsified medical products
2641c188b189.title: Digital transformation handbook for reporting substandard and falsified medical products
2641c188b189.content: World Health Organization (2026). Digital transformation handbook for reporting substandard and falsified medical products. World Health Organization. TitleDigital transformation handbook for reporting substandard and falsified medical products AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2026-6-9 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240120747 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThis handbook provides practical guidance to support countries in planning, designing and implementing digital solutions for reporting substandard and falsified medical products. These products pose a significant threat to public health, contributing to therapeutic failure, adverse effects, loss of trust in health systems and broader socioeconomic impacts. Effective detection and reporting are essential to enable regulatory authorities to investigate suspected cases, remove harmful products from circulation and contribute to global surveillance efforts through mechanisms such as WHO’s Global Surveillance and Monitoring System. The document outlines a structured approach to digital transformation, covering assessment of the current environment, stakeholder engagement, governance and policy alignment, definition of system requirements, implementation planning, and monitoring and evaluation. It emphasizes the transition from fragmented or paper-based reporting systems to interoperable digital platforms that improve data quality, standardization and timeliness. Drawing on global experience and existing WHO frameworks, the handbook promotes the use of user-centred design, open standards and integration with pharmacovigilance systems. It is intended for ministries of health, national regulatory authorities and partners seeking to strengthen reporting systems and enhance the capacity to detect and respond to substandard and falsified medical products. 3633e11606a2.title: Consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection: recommendations…
3633e11606a2.content: World Health Organization (2016). Consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection: recommendations for a public health approach. World Health Organization. TitleConsolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection: recommendations for a public health approach AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2016-6-6 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789241549684 Languageen AbstractThis evidence-based guideline consolidates World Health Organization recommendations on the use of antiretroviral (ARV) drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, providing a comprehensive public health framework for HIV diagnosis, prevention, treatment, service delivery, and monitoring and evaluation across all age groups and populations. Developed in response to advances in scientific evidence and evolving programmatic needs, the second edition updates the 2013 consolidated guidelines and incorporates new recommendations, including universal eligibility for antiretroviral therapy (ART) regardless of CD4 cell count, expanded use of pre-exposure prophylaxis, and optimized approaches to HIV testing, treatment monitoring and management of coinfections and comorbidities. The guideline also outlines the methods used for guideline development and the principles underpinning a public health approach. The publication provides evidence-based recommendations on HIV testing services, antiretroviral therapy, prevention interventions, differentiated service delivery models, linkage to care, adherence, decentralization, task sharing, laboratory services and programme monitoring. It emphasizes integrated, people-centred and community-based approaches to improve access to high-quality HIV services, strengthen health systems and support implementation in diverse epidemiological settings. Intended primarily for national HIV programme managers, clinicians, policy-makers and implementing partners, the guideline aims to accelerate progress towards universal access to HIV services and the global goal of ending the HIV epidemic as a major public health threat by 2030. 9331da7c452d.title: Global strategy on digital health 2020-2025
9331da7c452d.content: World Health Organization (2021). Global strategy on digital health 2020-2025. World Health Organization. TitleGlobal strategy on digital health 2020-2025 AuthorsWorld Health Organization Issued2021-8-18 Typebook PublisherWorld Health Organization ISBN9789240020924 (electronic version) Languageen AbstractThe Global strategy on digital health 2020–2025 provides a framework to support Member States in strengthening health systems through the appropriate adoption and use of digital technologies. Developed in response to World Health Assembly mandates and aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals and WHO’s Triple Billion targets, the strategy outlines a shared vision for improving health and well-being through accessible, affordable, secure and sustainable digital health solutions. It emphasizes the importance of strong governance, interoperability, ethical use of data, privacy protection, workforce capacity-building and investment in digital infrastructure to support national health priorities and universal health coverage. The document establishes four strategic objectives: promoting global collaboration and knowledge exchange; advancing the implementation of national digital health strategies; strengthening governance for digital health at global, regional and national levels; and advocating people-centred health systems enabled by digital technologies. It also presents guiding principles, an implementation framework and monitoring mechanisms to support countries in developing interoperable digital health ecosystems. Particular attention is given to addressing barriers faced by low- and middle-income countries and ensuring that digital transformation contributes to equitable, effective and resilient health systems.
